traceability.evidence:
Story file: - docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md exists and defines requirements REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION, REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION, REQ-PATH-FORMAT, REQ-REQ-FORMAT, REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT, REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING, REQ-ERROR-SPECIFICITY.
Core rule implementation: - src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts implements the ESLint rule that validates @story and @req annotation format and syntax. - The rule file is explicitly annotated with: - @story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md - @req REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION, REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION, REQ-PATH-FORMAT, REQ-REQ-FORMAT, REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT, REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING, REQ-ERROR-SPECIFICITY. - The rule follows ESLint best practices: - Exports `meta` with `type: "problem"`, `messages` using messageIds (`invalidStoryFormat`, `invalidReqFormat`, `invalidRuleConfiguration`), and `schema: getRuleSchema()`. - `create(context)` returns a `Program` visitor, which uses `context.getSourceCode().getAllComments()` to inspect all comments for @story/@req annotations.
Format & syntax validation (REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION, REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION): - `processComment` splits each comment into lines, normalizes them, and uses `processCommentLine` and `finalizePendingAnnotation` to build a `PendingAnnotation` object for @story/@req tags. - `validateStoryAnnotation` and `validateReqAnnotation` perform the actual syntax/format checks and call `context.report` with the appropriate messageId and data.
Path format validation (REQ-PATH-FORMAT): - src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-options.ts defines defaults: - `getDefaultStoryPattern(): /^docs\/stories\/[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-DEV-[\w-]+\.story\.md$/` - `getDefaultStoryExample(): "docs/stories/005.0-DEV-EXAMPLE.story.md"`. - `validateStoryAnnotation` uses `collapseAnnotationValue` to normalize multi-line values, then tests against `options.storyPattern`. - Errors are built with `buildStoryErrorMessage` (src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-utils.ts), producing: - Missing: `Missing story path for @story annotation. Expected a path like "docs/stories/005.0-DEV-EXAMPLE.story.md".` - Invalid: `Invalid story path "" for @story annotation. Expected a path like "docs/stories/005.0-DEV-EXAMPLE.story.md".` - Tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts cover: - `"[REQ-PATH-FORMAT] missing story path (single line)"` with `code: "// @story"` expecting `invalidStoryFormat` and the exact missing-path message. - `"[REQ-PATH-FORMAT] invalid story file extension"` and `"missing extension in story path"` verifying autofix to `.story.md` and correct error messages. - `"[REQ-PATH-FORMAT] story path must not use path traversal"` with `// @story ../docs/stories/...` reporting invalid format.
Requirement ID format validation (REQ-REQ-FORMAT): - Default requirement pattern and example: - `getDefaultReqPattern(): /^REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+$/` - `getDefaultReqExample(): "REQ-EXAMPLE"`. - `validateReqAnnotation` handles missing vs invalid IDs and reports `invalidReqFormat` with `buildReqErrorMessage("missing"|"invalid", ...)`. - `buildReqErrorMessage` produces: - Missing: `Missing requirement ID for @req annotation. Expected an identifier like "REQ-EXAMPLE".` - Invalid: `Invalid requirement ID "" for @req annotation. Expected an identifier like "REQ-EXAMPLE" (uppercase letters, numbers, and dashes only).` - Tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts include: - `"[REQ-REQ-FORMAT] missing req id (single line)"` with `// @req`. - `"[REQ-REQ-FORMAT] invalid req id format (single line)"` with `// @req invalid-format`. - `"[REQ-REQ-FORMAT] missing req identifier with trailing space"` with `// @req `.
Multiline support (REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT): - `collapseAnnotationValue(value: string)` in src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-utils.ts replaces all whitespace with `""`, so multi-line values become a single logical string. - `processCommentLine` accumulates continuation lines into `pending.value` when already inside a pending annotation. - `processComment` iterates all lines, normalizes each via `normalizeCommentLine`, and finalizes the pending annotation at the end. - Tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts validate multi-line behavior: - Valid: multi-line `@story` and `@req` examples in block comments (`[REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT]` tests). - Invalid: missing values and invalid values after collapsing whitespace, both for story and req.
Flexible parsing (REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING): - `normalizeCommentLine` trims lines, strips leading `*` for JSDoc lines, and if an `@story` or `@req` tag is present, slices from the tag index to the end, allowing tags to appear anywhere in the comment text. - This supports line comments (`//`), block comments (`/* */`), and JSDoc (`/** */`) with leading `*`. - tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts includes `[REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING]` test cases using JSDoc-style comments with leading `*` and variable whitespace, all treated as valid.
Error specificity & user experience (REQ-ERROR-SPECIFICITY): - `meta.messages.invalidStoryFormat` and `invalidReqFormat` are generic templates: `"Invalid annotation format: {{details}}."`. - Specificity is provided by `buildStoryErrorMessage` and `buildReqErrorMessage`, which: - Distinguish missing vs invalid values. - Echo the offending identifier/path (`"Invalid story path \"...\""`, `"Invalid requirement ID \"...\""`). - Embed example strings from configuration. - tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts asserts exact `data.details` strings for numerous invalid cases, including custom examples from user configuration.
Configuration & flexible patterns: - src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-options.ts defines `AnnotationRuleOptions` with nested `story`/`req` and flat shorthand fields (`storyPathPattern`, `storyPathExample`, `requirementIdPattern`, `requirementIdExample`). - `resolveOptions` uses `resolvePattern` and `resolveExample` to: - Generate RegExp instances from string patterns. - Accumulate optionErrors on invalid patterns with messages like `Invalid regular expression for option "story.pattern": "[unclosed"`. - Fall back to default patterns on error while still validating annotations. - src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts `create` function: - Calls `resolveOptions(context.options || [])` to obtain `options`. - Reads `getOptionErrors()` and, in `Program` visitor, reports each as `invalidRuleConfiguration` without stopping validation. - tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts verify these behaviors with cases like: - `[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-STORY]`, `[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-REQ]`, `[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-BOTH]` for nested options. - Flat shorthand tests for `storyPathPattern/Example` and `requirementIdPattern/Example`. - `[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-FALLBACK]` and `...-FLAT` for invalid regexes, both expecting `invalidRuleConfiguration` and a subsequent format error using default examples.
Integration with other rules (Integration acceptance criterion): - src/index.ts includes `"valid-annotation-format"` in `RULE_NAMES` and loads it dynamically from `./rules/valid-annotation-format`. - `TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES` maps `"traceability/valid-annotation-format"` to `"warn"`, aligning with formatting issues being warnings. - Function/branch rules (e.g., tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts, tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts, tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts) enforce presence of annotations, while valid-annotation-format validates their syntax and format. The rules operate on the same annotation style and are wired together through the plugin index.
Documentation (Documentation acceptance criterion): - docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md documents this rule and explicitly references the story and requirements: - `@story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md` - `@req REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION`, `REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION`, `REQ-PATH-FORMAT`, `REQ-REQ-FORMAT`. - The doc describes: - How the rule scans comments and supports multiline annotations. - Default and configurable formats for story paths and requirement IDs. - Example error messages for missing/invalid values. - Valid and invalid code examples matching the story’s examples.
Tests & traceability: - tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts header: - `Tests for: docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md`. - `@story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md` and `@req REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION ...` etc. - The `describe` block is named `"Valid Annotation Format Rule (Story 005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION)"` and individual tests reference specific requirements (e.g., `[REQ-PATH-FORMAT]`, `[REQ-REQ-FORMAT]`, `[REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT]`, `[REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING]`).
Plugin exposure: - README.md documents `traceability/valid-annotation-format` as: `Enforces correct format of traceability annotations. (Documentation: docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md)`. - This shows the rule is intended for user consumption and is properly wired into the plugin.
traceability.notes: The 005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION story is fully implemented. Error messages are specific and configurable via patterns and examples. All acceptance criteria and listed requirements for this story are satisfied based on concrete code and test evidence.
